title: Mobile App Security: Best Practices to Keep Your Customers Safe

image.alt: Mobile App Security: Best Practices to Keep Your Customers Safe

body.text: Mobile apps now handle payments, health records and private messages. From facilitating transactions to enhancing the customer experience, they have changed how companies work with their customers, and that makes them an attractive target. Security has to be designed in from day one.
1. Encrypt data in transit and at rest
Use TLS for every network call and never send sensitive data over plain HTTP. On the device, store secrets in the platform keychain or keystore rather than in plain files or shared preferences.

items: Support multi-factor authentication for sensitive actions.
Use short-lived tokens and refresh them securely.
Add biometric login where the device supports it.
Lock accounts or slow down attempts after repeated failures.

body.text: Validate all input, avoid hard-coded keys and keep third-party libraries up to date. Obfuscate release builds to make reverse engineering harder.
The app is only as safe as the server behind it. Authenticate and authorise every request on the server, rate-limit endpoints and never trust data that comes from the client.
Run automated scans in your build pipeline and schedule periodic penetration tests. Fix findings by severity and re-test after every major release.
Data you never collect cannot leak. Ask for the minimum permissions, explain why you need them and delete data you no longer require.
Security is a continuous practice, not a one-off task. Following these habits keeps your customers safe and protects your brand's reputation.
